subject: Banking
title: Central Bank Digital Currencies
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Central Bank Digital Currencies.

hook.text: China's digital yuan has been tested by 260 million people.

buildup.text: CBDCs are digital versions of national currencies issued directly by central banks.

discovery.text: CBDCs could eliminate bank runs. If people hold digital currency directly at the central bank.

twist.text: Privacy advocates warn that CBDCs give governments complete visibility into every transaction. Cash is anonymous.

climax.text: CBDCs promise efficiency but threaten privacy. The design choices embed political values into the money itself.

punchline.text: 260 million testers. Government digital money trades efficiency for privacy.

quiz.question: What privacy concern surrounds CBDCs?
options: Governments can track every single transaction made with digital currency

details.summary: Central bank digital currencies in the context of future banking represent a potential transformation where government-issued digital money operates alongside or replaces commercial bank deposits, reshaping the entire banking system's structure.
details.whyItMatters: If consumers hold money directly with the central bank via CBDC, they may no longer need commercial bank deposits. This could drain banks of their primary funding source and force a complete rethinking of how banking works.
takeaways: CBDCs could disintermediate commercial banks from the deposit business
Central banks are designing CBDCs to avoid destabilizing the banking system
Holding limits and zero-interest CBDCs aim to prevent bank deposit flight

faq.question: Could CBDCs cause a bank run?
faq.answer: In theory, yes. If people can instantly move all deposits from commercial banks to a risk-free central bank digital wallet, any loss of confidence could trigger rapid mass withdrawals. This is why most CBDC designs include holding limits.

faq.question: How would banks fund loans without deposits?
faq.answer: Banks would need alternative funding sources like wholesale markets or central bank lending facilities. Some CBDC designs route transactions through commercial banks specifically to maintain their intermediary role and lending capacity.
